label: delimiter step of long sequences, about to output s/t/j/y/r/g first
explanation: Almost never active in the original phase (0.1% of mass). 67% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (8% of delimiter steps fire), and most of the rest is in early copy steps (recall_idx 1-3). Firing rate rises with L and to_go (9.4x lift at to_go=8), and depends strongly on which token is being output: s, t, j, y, r and g give 4-9x lift, while digits 0/3 and b/u are weak. The top activations are all at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences whose first token is s/t/j/y/r, often followed by weaker firing on the next copy step. The predicate (delimiter, L>=7, out_tok in that set) reaches only about 0.4 precision and 0.32 recall on dev, so the unit reads as a graded, distributed code of output identity times remaining length, not a clean boolean feature. Adding copy-phase steps with the same output set raises mass recall to about 0.5-0.6 but lowers F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (copy phase: s, t, j, y; delimiter step: s, t, j, y; input phase: ) and the input two steps back (most: 0, o, w, q, l, f; least: j, s, t, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=8 & t=7, L=9.
